panels.description: Wide, full page width. Padmini Amma's estate at midday in the monsoon season. Beyond the red-tiled roofs and coconut palms, a bank of heavy cloud is building in the north. In the inner courtyard, in the deep shade of the big jackfruit tree, Nagoji sits on the worn stone platform. He dresses as Ananthan Pillai now: Kerala topknot with the first grey at the temples, NO turban, a plain white mundu with no gold border and a shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife with the conch mark at his waist, the silver chain of office on his chest. Clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud. Beyond the low wall, boys spar in the kalari pit.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: News from the Deccan arrived the way monsoon storms do.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not as a single, clear front, but as a series of clouds that thickened until you realised the sky had changed.

panels.description: Padmini, walking stick in one hand, tossing a small cloth-wrapped bundle into Nagoji's lap with the other. In her fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for walking. Her face is softer than usual. Nagoji at the edge of frame (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain).

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: From your hills, my son.

panels.description: Padmini glancing back over her shoulder at the kitchen steps. A thin, sun-blackened Deccan village boy squats there with a coarse black wool blanket over one shoulder and cracked, dusty bare feet, shovelling rice from a leaf as fast as his hand can move.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The boy who brought it walked like a man used to stones, not sand.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He eats too fast. That is how I know he comes from a place where grain is a worry.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's hands unwrapping the cloth. Fine grey-black Deccan dust sifts out of the folds onto his white mundu. The fingernails have grown back ridged and discoloured, and the old Portuguese brand shows as a pale ridged scar on his left wrist (raised ridges only, no letters). The fingers are not quite steady.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a long time after Goa and the storm, I had trained myself not to look north too often.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then a letter arrived with my village's dust still clinging to it.

panels.description: Insert. A folded sheet of paper, not palm leaf, opening in his hands. Lines of dense handwriting drawn as ink marks only, nothing readable.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My name, in a hand I recognised even before I read the words.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My younger brother Bhalerao's, grown more angular since I had last seen it.

panels.description: Wide. The land near Nashik at dawn: black-soil fields cracked and waiting for rain, a low stone village with flat roofs behind them, dry flat-topped hills beyond, a pale sky. Two tiny figures at the far edge of a field. No named character in close view.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter, Bhalerao's hand)
copy.text: Nagoji anna. We heard from a trader that you did not drown. I would have been offended if the sea had kept you. This land needs you more than salt does.

panels.description: Nagoji's parents at the edge of the field, both white-haired and bent with age. His father, thick-knuckled, in a coarse dhoti, a white pheta and a black wool kambal over one shoulder, a wooden plough balanced on the other shoulder, squints up at a cloudless white sky with his free hand shading his eyes. His mother beside him in a nine-yard sari worn kashta-style, green glass bangles on her wrists, a seed basket on her hip, one hand raised mid-argument.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Our parents live. Their backs bend more than before.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Father says the sky is more unreliable than the Peshwa. I am not sure which is the greater insult.

panels.description: Wide. A Deccan hill fort on a flat-topped scarp. On the dusty road below it, two small bands of Maratha riders pass each other going opposite ways, each under its own pennant: one a saffron swallow-tailed Maratha pennant, the other a plain dark red pennant. No emblems, no crescents, no lettering on either. The riders eye each other across the gap, hands resting near their sword hilts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Our forts still stand, but their banners change more often.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Some say the Maratha hand is strong. Others say each finger pulls in a different direction.

panels.description: Back to the present, full colour, under the jackfruit tree. Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) reading, the sheet near its end. The small smile the earlier lines gave him is going out of his face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Do you remember Keshavrao, who sat in the cell with you near the coast before they took you away?

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face (topknot greying at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, gold ear stud), the paper at the bottom of frame. His eyes are wet and unblinking, his jaw tight. The ink marks on the paper at the bottom edge are drawn slightly smeared and soft, as if seen through tears.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: We heard a tale from a coastal trader that a boy with his name died trying to escape a Portuguese ship.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: There are many boys and many names. Stories change as they travel. I do not know if this is true.

panels.description: The back of Nagoji's head at the panel edge, and bleeding in behind it like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame (the Chapter 1, panel 6.5 technique): the storm from Chapter 3, black water boiling around the ship's hull, and a rope stretched taut across the heeled deck toward the flooded hatch.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We heard a tale.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not a report. Not a record. A story. Yet stories carry their own weight.

panels.description: Flashback, tight. Keshavrao in the water: young, narrow shoulders, black hair hacked short, torn prisoner rags, iron manacles on his thin wrists, a rain-washed graze at the hairline (no blood drawn), eyes wide, mouth open. The snapped end of the rope floats slack beside him as a wave rises over his head.
Present. Tight on Nagoji's thumb pressed flat against the paper, the knuckle pale, the ridged nail catching the light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had known, in my bones, that the sea had kept him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Seeing the shape of the tale written in my brother's hand pressed that knowledge into ink.

panels.description: Wide, back in the letter's palette. A darbar hall in Pune. Maratha sardars in pagdis and angarkhas sit around a hand-painted cloth map in the Indian style spread on the floor: rivers as blue bands, forts as small pictograms, no coastline outline of the subcontinent, NO lettering anywhere on it. They are split: one leans back with folded arms, one spreads his hands in admiration, and one man's finger presses down hard on the bottom edge of the cloth, where the painted rivers run out into a band of sea. No one here is a named portrait.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: The Peshwa's court has heard of a southern king who broke white men on a beach.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Some say we should conquer him before he grows too strong.

panels.description: Wide. Afternoon. The shade has moved across the courtyard. Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) tucks the folded letter into the waist of his mundu. The estate goes on around him: women calling across the yard, boys in the kalari, a servant with a brass pot. Padmini stands a respectful distance off, leaning on her stick.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Deccan names wrapped themselves around Travancore sounds in my head until it felt as if two different songs were playing at once.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Bad news?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Mixed. Which is the only kind that travels far.

panels.description: Two-shot. Padmini has come close and looks down at him, stick planted. Nagoji seated on the stone platform (topknot greying at the temples, plain white mundu, silver chain).

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Your people live.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes. For now.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And the men who rule your hills?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They grow sharper. And more divided.

panels.description: Padmini alone, nodding once.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Sharp and divided. Dangerous combination.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her words should have steadied me.

panels.description: Dusk in the same inner courtyard, the light going blue. In the foreground, Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain) rises from the stone platform under the jackfruit tree. In the background, a court runner comes in through the courtyard entrance, breathing hard: younger and wiry, bare-chested with no shoulder cloth and no chain, a short white mundu hitched to the knee, hair in a small knot, a thin runner's staff in his hand, dust to the shins.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Instead, I heard Ibrahim's voice. The wind blows in circles, and names travel.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: The Maharaja wants you. Bring the letter.

panels.description: Wide. A small lamp-lit room off the war hall. Shelves of palm-leaf bundles, a few cloth-wrapped European volumes that were once Portuguese property, rolled maps. On the left, Marthanda Varma (V13 varma-v1 face; court dress: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, pearl drop earrings, red vertical forehead mark, pearl and gold necklaces, gold armlets, bare-chested, cream cloth with a broad gold border) sits on a low platform holding the letter. On the right, Nagoji sits on a mat below him: bare head with his topknot greying at the temples, no forehead mark, plain white mundu with no gold border, shoulder cloth, the silver chain, the conch-marked knife. No guards in frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Your brother has a quick mind. I like his joke about the sky and the Peshwa.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He does not have to face either directly. That makes jokes easier.

panels.description: Varma (peacock-crest turban, pearl earrings, forehead mark), a faint smile, already fading.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Maratha confederacy is a storm with many centres. What interests me is this.

panels.description: Insert. The king's forefinger, a gold ring on it, tapping one line near the foot of the page. Ink marks only, nothing readable.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: "Conquer him before he grows too strong."

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you think they will try?

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, plain white mundu, silver chain), eyes lowered, working it through.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If they think you are weak, yes.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If they think you are useful, they will keep you as you are, so long as you do not interfere with their plans. They have many enemies closer to home.

panels.description: Varma on the platform (left, peacock-crest turban, gold armlets) leaning forward; Nagoji on the mat (right, bare-headed topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain). The lamp burns behind the king and throws his shadow across the mat and over Nagoji.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And you?

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If they sent a letter with your brother, ordering you back under their banner, what would you do?

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) from a low angle, the lamp in the foreground. Bleeding in behind his head like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: a Deccan fort wall of dark stone with iron cannon in its embrasures. Only this one stain.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words landed like weights on the mat between us.

panels.description: Nagoji meets the king's eyes. Measured.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I would read the letter. I would weigh it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I would remember Goa. I would remember the storm. I would remember Colachel. Then I would choose.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Nagoji's hand at his waist, resting on the ivory hilt of the knife with the conch mark, the thumb laid over the conch and gone still. Not gripping. Ridged nails.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You do not say which way you would choose.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Because I am not arrogant enough to think I know what the world will look like when that letter arrives.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If it arrives.

panels.description: Varma on the platform (left, peacock-crest turban, pearl earrings, forehead mark) sets the letter down beside him, studying Nagoji on the mat (right, bare-headed topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Honest. I prefer honest answers to pious lies.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Understand this, Ananthan. You are useful to me because you are Maratha and because you are Padmini's son.

panels.description: Varma leaning in toward the lamp, lit from below, his gaze sharpening. Peacock-crest turban, pearl earrings, forehead mark.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You can speak to men in Pune in a way my other nobles cannot.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You can make them fear and respect this kingdom, or you can make them see it as prey.

panels.description: Wide two-shot from the side, low, at mat level. Varma on the platform (left, peacock-crest turban, gold armlets), Nagoji on the mat (right, bare-headed topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain). The lamp burns behind the king, and his shadow lies across the mat in a dark band between the two men, stopping just short of Nagoji's knees.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you ever choose the second, we will stand on opposite sides of a very narrow river.

panels.description: Wide. Seen from the dark corridor outside, looking through the open doorway into the lamp-lit room. In the corridor's shadow in the foreground stand two Nair officers (bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, hair in a front knot, curved Nair swords at the hip, no shoulder cloth, no chain, no European coat), watching. Through the doorway, Varma leans back on his platform with a faint half-smile, flicking one hand to dismiss the solemnity, and Nagoji (topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain) rises from the mat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you choose the first, you will have my gratitude. For whatever that is worth.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: For now, you stay. The north will have to wait its turn.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The shadows of the Deccan had lengthened into Travancore's corridors.

panels.description: Wide. Day, some days later. A fort yard where men load bullock carts with supplies for a northern fort. The same two Nair officers in the foreground turn their heads to follow Nagoji as he passes in the midground, weighing him. Nagoji's topknot greying at the temples and his silver chain are clearly visible; plain white mundu, no turban. Padmini walks beside him with her stick, watching the carts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the days that followed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not mistrust exactly. More calculation.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You cannot stand with one foot in each river forever. At some point you must choose which current to let carry you.

panels.description: Two-shot, Padmini and Nagoji (topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain), the carts rolling out through the fort gate behind them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What if I cling to a rock between them?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Then you drown slower. But you still drown.

panels.description: Wide. Evening. The verandah of the Velinadu house, carved wooden pillars, lamps just lit. Revathi (indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, no tali) stands facing Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain), arms folded.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Your hills call you. Your king here calls you. You are flattered to be wanted by both.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Neither will mourn very long if they must cut you loose.

panels.description: Closer two-shot. Nagoji's mouth tight; Revathi unmoved, chin up.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have a cruel tongue.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: No. I have an impatient one.

panels.description: Revathi leaning back against a carved pillar, a playful glint in her eyes, glancing down at the silver chain on Nagoji's chest.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Besides, do not let that silver chain weigh you down with too much hope.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Even if you have a tharavadu now, I am a Princess of Velinadu. We do not marry commoners, Nagoji. Even ones who think they have found a root.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face in the lamplight (topknot greying at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, gold ear stud). The half-smile he gave her is still on his mouth, and it has left his eyes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was said in jest, but the wall was there, invisible and ancient.

panels.description: Wide. Night. Moonlight over coconut palms. Irrigation channels glint between the trees. Nagoji (topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain) sits alone on the edge of the verandah of his quarters.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That impatient tongue was right. I could not stand in two rivers.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That night, I did not sleep.

panels.description: Close on his hands held out, palms up, in the moonlight. The nails have grown back ridged and discoloured. The old Portuguese brand is a pale ridged scar on the left wrist (raised ridges, no letters), and faint healed rope scars cross both palms. No fresh wounds.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: These hands had held Maratha reins on Deccan dust. They had gripped Portuguese chains in Goa's darkness.

panels.description: The same hands, and behind them, bleeding in as a stain: the storm from Chapter 3. Nagoji's bandaged palms in iron manacles (captivity-era hands, not the present look), the rope tearing through the cloth, and at its far end Keshavrao's thin manacled hand gripping the hatch frame. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had pulled Keshavrao toward a rope that broke.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had trained Travancore cavalry in wet sand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Whose hands were they now?

panels.description: Three narrow insets side by side across one strip, each showing only hands. His father's old, thick-knuckled hands on a plough handle. His mother's old hands, green glass bangles and turmeric stains, on a flat grinding stone, rolling the stone roller at dawn. His younger brother's slim, ink-stained fingers at a cotton angarkha cuff, scratching a line with a reed pen by lamplight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They did not know the man those hands had made me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They remembered a son who rode north and never came home.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That man had been simpler. He had known which rivers were his.

panels.description: Wide. The night sea off this coast, seen at the waterline and below it: a thin line of moonlit surface at the top, and beneath it, in the black water, the broken timbers of a wrecked ship, a split spar and loose planks settling on the sand. No bones, no body, no figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had followed me. He had trusted me. And I had let go.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I could not bring him back. But I could stop pretending that the man who failed him still existed.

panels.description: Back on the verandah, the moon lower. Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, plain white mundu, silver chain) on his feet, reaching into the wall niche beside the door to turn up the wick of a small brass lamp. The flame climbs and throws warm light across his face. No writing board in this panel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The decision arrived not as a thunderclap but as a settling, like silt finding the riverbed after a flood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now I would let it carry me.

panels.description: Wide. Morning at the harbour market: fish baskets, pepper sacks, masts beyond the roofs. A Gujarati sowcar's stall under a cloth awning. The money changer sits cross-legged on a platform spread with white cloth, in a small red pagdi and white angarkha, with a balance scale, a cloth-bound ledger, a small brass inkpot and a reed pen (kalam). Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) sets a heavy leather pouch down in front of him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Gold from Padmini Amma's private vault. A debt I would repay with service, or blood.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: This goes to Nashik. To the house of Ramji Sawant.

panels.description: The sowcar weighing the pouch on his palm, eyebrows lifting at the heft, his other hand pointing at a folded letter sealed with wax that lies on the white cloth beside the scale. Nagoji across the platform from him (topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain).

copy.speaker: SOWCAR
copy.text: It is a long road, Karyakkar. Roads have bandits. Bandits have hunger.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It travels by your hundi. Your paper is worth more than gold on the road.

copy.speaker: SOWCAR
copy.text: And this?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: This travels with it.

panels.description: Flashback to the night before, warm and dim. Over Nagoji's shoulder at a low writing board: a sheet of paper, his hand moving a reed pen (kalam) across it, a small brass inkpot, the brass lamp burning high beside it. Lines of ink marks only, nothing readable.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter, Nagoji's hand)
copy.text: To Bhalerao Sawant.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: The man known as Nagoji died at Colachel. The sea that took Keshavrao took him too, in a different way.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Do not look for him. He fights battles that are no longer yours.

panels.description: Insert, tight. The reed pen's tip moving along a line of ink marks, the page half filled, the lamplight lower and redder now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Use this gold to buy new seed, to fix the roof, to keep the creditors from the door. It is the last debt he owed you.

panels.description: Insert, tight. The same sheet, finished, a last line of ink marks at the bottom. The reed pen laid across the brass inkpot. The lamp flame beside it has shrunk to a bead.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter)
copy.text: Forget his name. Remember his love.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was a lie. And it was the truest thing I had ever written.

panels.description: Insert, back at the stall in daylight. The sowcar's brass seal pressing down into a blob of red wax on the folded hundi. Ink marks only.

copy.speaker: SOWCAR
copy.text: It will reach them. My word is iron.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: See that it is.

panels.description: Wide. Padmini's estate gate in late afternoon, the light going gold toward dusk, long shadows across the path, the first lamp glowing inside the red-tiled tharavadu behind the gate. Padmini waits at the gate, leaning on her stick. Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) arrives on foot, empty-handed. Her eyes are on his empty hands.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Lighter, as if I had cut a heavy pack from my saddle.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The letter is sent?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes.

panels.description: Over Padmini's shoulder onto Nagoji's face in the low gold light. He glances back down the road toward the market.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And the man who wrote it?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He stayed at the market. He is not coming back.

panels.description: Close on Padmini, her eyes searching his, the last gold light on her face.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Then who stands before me?

panels.description: Tight. Nagoji's left hand closing on the silver chain of office at his chest: ridged nails against the cold metal, faint scars across the palm, the brand on the wrist. Dusk light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment, I felt the pull of two currents.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, no turban, plain white mundu, silver chain) at the gate, the wind lifting his shoulder cloth. Padmini at the left edge of the frame, only her shoulder and her stick in view. Behind him the image splits with no border between the halves: on one side the dry Deccan, black soil and dust on the wind; on the other this coast, wet palms, pepper vines and surf. No animals, no figures in either half.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now, standing at this gate, I let one of them go.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not forgotten. Never forgotten. But released, the way you release a horse too old to ride, with gratitude and grief.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face (topknot greying at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, gold ear stud), level, speaking to her.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The scars would remain. But the name attached to them could.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Ananthan Pillai.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The man I had been died in the black water with Keshavrao. The sea had just taken longer to tell me.

panels.description: Padmini smiling, an expression that cracks the iron mask she usually wears. Dusk light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: New and stiff like unconquered leather. But it fit.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Welcome home, Ananthan Pillai. Dinner is ready. Do not make us wait.

panels.description: Insert, small. Padmini turning toward the gate. At her waistband, a narrow palm-leaf ola letter tied with red thread, one end darkened by lamp smoke. Nothing written is visible.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi's latest letter. The thought that my new name might one day be spoken in her halls lodged itself like a small, dangerous hope.

panels.description: Wide, full width, the last panel of the chapter. Nagoji (topknot, plain white mundu, silver chain) follows Padmini through the gate into the courtyard at dusk, the jackfruit tree ahead and the lamps being lit along the verandah.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Deccan son was gone. Another man, with two coasts in his chest, had taken his place.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the moment, that was enough.
